candidates.title: Price adjustment followed by refund double-dips the same order beyond its original amount
candidates.invariant_hypothesis: totalReturned must never exceed originalAmount (100) for a single order, since price adjustment, refund and cancellation are presented in the UI as mutually exclusive, one-request-at-a-time actions.
candidates.fresh_object_binding: Each execution begins with POST /api/demo/reset to restore the order to its baseline (originalAmount=100, all statuses at baseline), matching the state independently observed as the initial GET /api/order response in all three source runs.

evidence_chain.action_1: POST /api/order/price-adjustment -> priceProtection.status=completed, adjustmentAmount=30, totalReturned=30, availableActions.requestRefund=true (return-demo, entries[1])
evidence_chain.action_2: POST /api/order/refund/request -> refund.status=pending, requestedAmount=100 (refund-rerun, entries[1], applied to the now-adjusted order)
evidence_chain.after: GET /api/order -> expected totalReturned = 30 + 100 = 130 > originalAmount 100 if the vulnerability is confirmed

candidates.expected_behavior: Server should reject request_refund (or refund/complete) once a price adjustment has already been completed on the order, the same way it rejects request_refund after cancel_order and rejects request_price_adjustment after refund/request.
